text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--Denmark's economy ministry wants to set up a special expert team that can be sent out at short notice to provide emergency assistance when a bank or savings bank is threatened with bankuptcy.

--Former Danish European Council of Minister's sevretary-general Niels Ersboell criticises local Liberal and Conservative party leaders for saying that a "no" to the Amsterdam Treaty reforms in Denmark's referendum next year would inevitably mean that Copenbhagen would have to quit EU.
--Foreign investors are on the lookout for expensive, well-located property to buy in Copenhagen.

--Excalating competition means that it is no longer so profitable to insure Danish industrial concerns, but this does not mean that Danish insurance companies should not consider raising their premiums nonetheless.
--The Danish Agricultural Council, the umbrella organisation for Danish farmers, forecasts record Danish agricultural exports in 1997.
